chunks: Saʿd, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about wearing silk and brocade, and he said: “As for in war, there is no objection, even if there are images in it.”

It is also possible that what he عليه السلام meant was when the brocade had warp and weft of spun thread or linen, without being pure silk throughout, because whenever the matter is like that, salat in it is permissible. And there is nothing in the report stating that it was brocade containing nothing of spun thread nor of linen; rather, it allows the possibility of what we have mentioned. And that which indicates what we have said is what he narrated:

key_terms.الدِّيبَاجِ: brocade, a fine woven fabric mentioned alongside silk
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), whose validity in such clothing is being addressed
key_terms.الْحَرِيرِ: silk, whose use is under consideration here
key_terms.الْحَرْبِ: warfare, the circumstance in which concession is stated
key_terms.تَمَاثِيلُ: images or figures present in the fabric
key_terms.سَدَاهُ: the warp of the woven cloth
key_terms.لَحْمَتُهُ: the weft of the woven cloth
key_terms.لِبَاسِ: garment or clothing being discussed in the legal ruling

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to wear silk or brocade, and can one pray in such clothing according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on wearing silk and brocade, stating that there is no objection to it in warfare even if it contains images. The appended legal discussion explains that the report may refer to brocade mixed with thread or linen, in which case salat in it would be permissible, showing a juristic effort to reconcile the narration with broader legal principles.
